newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco studies expansion at Radomiro Tomic.
newsitem.headline: Codelco studies expansion at Radomiro Tomic.

text.p: Chilean state copper company Codelco has begun studies to raise production at its half-built Radomiro Tomic copper mine to up to 290,000 tonnes a year, said the mine's general manager Luis Farias.
"We are carrying out internal studies to see what our best option is. We are looking at a range of options from 170,000 tonnes to 290,000 tonnes a year," he told reporters.
Radomiro Tomic is due to produce about 150,000 tonnes of copper when it comes into full production in February 1998.
Farias said Codelco is carrying out pre-feasibility studies on the options, and that any expansion was likely to take place in about 2000 or 2001.
Expansion to about 250,000 tonnes would cost an additional $150 million, on top of the $641 million it will cost Codelco to build the mine as it's now planned, he said.

Farias said building work at the mine, lying north of the Chuquicamata pit in arid northern Chile, is ahead of schedule. By the end of November, 51 percent of the work had been completed against 41 percent on the original timetable.
He reported a ''significant advance'' in building the mine and that it could come on stream earlier than planned.
"It's more than likely there will be an advance in the production startup date," he said, but declined to give details on when.

Radomiro Tomic is the first mine Codelco has built from scratch and will be operated as the company's fifth division. Its four other mines were all nationalized from foreign companies in the early 1970s.
